_comment: Make or rename this file for 'mcp_config.json'.
FORMAT
Compatible with Claude Desktop and Cursor out of the box.
Copy an existing mcpServers block from those clients and it will work.
OPTIONAL 'affordance' BLOCK
Add an 'affordance' block to any server entry to control how its tools
are exposed inside the DigiPet framework. All fields are optional.
Servers without an affordance block default to always_available with
no item or room gating — all tools exposed, nothing hidden.
affordance fields
use_level     : 'always_available' | 'dual_use' | 'room_only' | 'inventory_only'
item_types    : list of item type strings — agent must have/see one to access tools
room_types    : list of room type strings — agent must be in a matching room
include_tools : whitelist of tool names — omit or [] means ALL tools
exclude_tools : blacklist of tool names — omit or [] means NOTHING hidden
inject_prompts: list[str]  parameterless prompts only — rendered at context-build time as agent_information
prompt_tools:   list[str]  prompts WITH arguments — exposed as callable tools the agent can invoke
PRIORITY
Python-declared servers/affordances in tool_registry.py always take
precedence over entries here if registry keys clash.
EXTERNAL RUNTIMES
stdio servers that use 'npx' require Node.js to be installed.
See MCP_SERVERS.md for per-server prerequisites.
Simple example, uses a new 'mcp_colab' server by Google. Just the command needed, will resolve to .venv bin path.
see https://github.com/googlecolab/colab-mcp for details.
Install in project root: pip install git+https://github.com/googlecolab/colab-mcp
command gets resolved to the executable in your Python environment.

affordance._comment: Needs an item either in the room or inventory with type 'colab_endpoint' to access tools.

_comment: Using docker to run a GitHub MCP server image. Requires Docker installed and configured.
see https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server for details.
Required to set GitHub token in .env file, 'GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN', scope its permissions, preferably create it to read-only access, here a server is initialized with Read-Only functions.
We take no responsibility for how you set up your token or Github permissions, be careful!
Just make sure you set your token, Docker is running, and the server will get ready on first load.

tamagotchi_mcp._comment: Example of an MCP server running as a local web service. Just needs the URL and an item type to gate access. (or 'always_available' if you want it open all the time, not recommended for most integrations!. Maybe if you want to run... a memory MCP use case?)
